question: Does the frozen-fixture measurement depend on the node ids, and would replacing one fixed id with a generated one move a number? (Mutation D of the Fatia 2 table.)
how: Each frozen fixture measured three ways through the production path (irToLayoutGraph -> layoutElkGraph -> readElkHandleOrder -> measureRenderedReadability), with --retry=0: as-is; with every id prefixed 'zz-'; and with every id remapped to a rank token that inverts the lexical order. IR array order untouched in all three.

singleIdSubstitution.what: B-run1: "az-a" replaced by "n-7f3c91a2" at every occurrence.
singleIdSubstitution.result: generated-diagrams.baseline.test.ts — 10 passed. No measured number moved.

conclusion: The measurement is insensitive to the value of an id and to a uniform rename; it is sensitive to the relative order of the ids. Mutation D as written — one fixed id swapped for a generated-looking one — therefore does NOT break the stability test, and is recorded as a mutation that did not bite. The fixtures reproduce because they are frozen literals in declaration order.
orderPermutationNote: All six measured. The permutation is not uniformly an improvement or a regression: rendered crossings fall for A-run1 (10->5), A-run3 (51->43), B-run1 (23->11) and B-run2 (99->55), rise in ELK's own count for A-run1 (1->2) and B-run3 (52->60), and B-run2's ELK count falls hard (33->11). Renaming nothing but the ids moves the layout by more than most layout changes would. That instability is a Fatia 3 concern; it is recorded here because it is what makes freezing the fixtures worth doing.
